speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a scalp and forehead rash; to help me understand this, have you noticed any itching, pain, or changes in your hair or eyebrows?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Scraping; REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp_and_Forehead_Rash

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Scraping: Microscopy - No signs of fungal infection; Culture - Negative for bacterial growth

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis. The combination of erythematous patches, greasy yellow scales, and worsening in cold weather is classic for this condition, not tuberculosis as previously suggested. I have requested a skin scraping and images to confirm the findings and rule out other causes.
